/*
 * ======================================================================
 *  VD BACKUP  ::  root backup & restore, no grant prompt
 *  Full app/data backup & restore as root - KernelSU/APatch/Magisk WebUI.
 *
 *  Copyright (C) 2026  VD171
 *  SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 *  Free software under the GNU AGPL v3 or later. NETWORK COPYLEFT: run a
 *  modified version, even as a service, and you MUST offer its source.
 *
 *  Site           : https://vd171.ru
 *  Site           : https://vd.priv8.ru
 *  Source         : https://github.com/VD171/VD-Backup
 *  GitHub         : @VD171 https://github.com/VD171
 *  XDA-Developers : @VD171 https://xdaforums.com/m/vd171.4699873/
 *  XDA-Thread     : https://xdaforums.com/t/VD-Backup.4807267/
 *  Telegram       : @VD_Priv8 https://t.me/VD_Priv8
 *  Telegram       : @Priv8_VD https://t.me/Priv8_VD
 *  Discord        : @VD.Priv8 https://discord.com/users/1296831918989639721
 *  E-mail         : vd.priv8@pm.me
 * ======================================================================
 */
package ru.vd171.vdbackup

import android.app.Notification
import android.app.NotificationChannel
import android.app.NotificationManager
import android.app.Service
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.content.pm.ServiceInfo
import android.os.Build
import android.os.IBinder

class DriveCommandService : Service() {

    override fun onBind(intent: Intent?): IBinder? = null

    override fun onStartCommand(intent: Intent?, flags: Int, startId: Int): Int {
        promoteForeground()
        if (intent == null) {
            stopSelfResult(startId)
            return START_NOT_STICKY
        }
        val op = intent.getStringExtra("op") ?: ""
        val src = intent.getStringExtra("src")
        val dst = intent.getStringExtra("dst")
        val id = intent.getStringExtra("id")
        val name = intent.getStringExtra("name")
        val result = intent.getStringExtra("result")
        Thread {
            runOp(op, src, dst, id, name, result)
            stopForegroundCompat()
            stopSelfResult(startId)
        }.start()
        return START_NOT_STICKY
    }

    private fun runOp(op: String, src: String?, dst: String?, id: String?, name: String?, result: String?) {
        val client = DriveClient(this)
        try {
            when (op) {
                "check" -> {
                    val ok = client.checkConsent()
                    emit(result, ok, op, if (ok) "ERR_NONE" else "ERR_NO_CONSENT", null, "consent status")
                }
                "list" -> emit(result, true, op, "ERR_NONE", client.list(name), "list ok")
                "upload" -> {
                    val source = src ?: ""
                    val remote = if (!name.isNullOrEmpty()) name else source.substringAfterLast('/')
                    emit(result, true, op, "ERR_NONE", client.upload(source, remote), "upload ok")
                }
                "download" -> emit(result, true, op, "ERR_NONE", client.download(id ?: "", dst ?: ""), "download ok")
                "delete" -> emit(result, true, op, "ERR_NONE", client.delete(id ?: ""), "delete ok")
                else -> emit(result, false, op, "ERR_UNKNOWN_OP", null, "unknown op")
            }
        } catch (e: DriveClient.DriveException) {
            emit(result, false, op, e.code, null, e.message)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            emit(result, false, op, "ERR_INTERNAL", null, e.message)
        }
    }

    private fun emit(result: String?, ok: Boolean, op: String, code: String, data: String?, message: String?) {
        result?.let { CommandResult.write(it, ok, op, code, data, message) }
    }

    private fun promoteForeground() {
        val nm = getSystemService(Context.NOTIFICATION_SERVICE) as NotificationManager
        if (nm.getNotificationChannel(CHANNEL_ID) == null) {
            nm.createNotificationChannel(
                NotificationChannel(CHANNEL_ID, "VDBackup Drive", NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_MIN)
            )
        }
        val notification: Notification = Notification.Builder(this, CHANNEL_ID)
            .setContentTitle(getString(R.string.companion_service_label))
            .setSmallIcon(android.R.drawable.stat_sys_upload)
            .build()
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.Q) {
            startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification, ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC)
        } else {
            startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification)
        }
    }

    private fun stopForegroundCompat() {
        stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE)
    }

    companion object {
        private const val CHANNEL_ID = "vdbackup_companion"
        private const val NOTIFICATION_ID = 1
    }
}

/*

 *  Full app/data backup & restore as root - KernelSU/APatch/Magisk WebUI.
 *
 *  Copyright (C) 2026  VD171

 *  modified version, even as a service, and you MUST offer its source.
 *
 *  Site           : https://vd171.ru
 *  Site           : https://vd.priv8.ru
 *  Source         : https://github.com/VD171/VD-Backup
 *  GitHub         : @VD171 https://github.com/VD171
 *  XDA-Developers : @VD171 https://xdaforums.com/m/vd171.4699873/
 *  XDA-Thread     : https://xdaforums.com/t/VD-Backup.4807267/
 *  Telegram       : @VD_Priv8 https://t.me/VD_Priv8
 *  Telegram       : @Priv8_VD https://t.me/Priv8_VD
 *  Discord        : @VD.Priv8 https://discord.com/users/1296831918989639721
 *  E-mail         : vd.priv8@pm.me
 * ======================================================================
 */
package ru.vd171.vdbackup

import android.accounts.Account
import android.content.Context

object TokenStore {
    private const val PREFS = "vdbackup_companion"
    private const val KEY_ACCOUNT = "account_name"

    fun saveAccount(context: Context, name: String?) {
        context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
            .edit().putString(KEY_ACCOUNT, name).apply()
    }

    fun accountName(context: Context): String? =
        context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE).getString(KEY_ACCOUNT, null)

    fun account(context: Context): Account? =
        accountName(context)?.let { Account(it, DriveConfig.ACCOUNT_TYPE) }

    fun clear(context: Context) {
        context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE).edit().remove(KEY_ACCOUNT).apply()
    }
}

#
#   Gradle start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh Gradle
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/HEAD/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s
' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac

CLASSPATH=$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar


# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )
    CLASSPATH=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$CLASSPATH" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 "-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -classpath "$CLASSPATH" \
        org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ======================================================================
#  VD BACKUP  ::  root backup & restore, no grant prompt
#  Full app/data backup & restore as root - KernelSU/APatch/Magisk WebUI.
#
#  Copyright (C) 2026  VD171
#  SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
#
#  Free software under the GNU AGPL v3 or later. NETWORK COPYLEFT: run a
#  modified version, even as a service, and you MUST offer its source.
#
#  Site           : https://vd171.ru
#  Site           : https://vd.priv8.ru
#  Source         : https://github.com/VD171/VD-Backup
#  GitHub         : @VD171 https://github.com/VD171
#  XDA-Developers : @VD171 https://xdaforums.com/m/vd171.4699873/
#  XDA-Thread     : https://xdaforums.com/t/VD-Backup.4807267/
#  Telegram       : @VD_Priv8 https://t.me/VD_Priv8
#  Telegram       : @Priv8_VD https://t.me/Priv8_VD
#  Discord        : @VD.Priv8 https://discord.com/users/1296831918989639721
#  E-mail         : vd.priv8@pm.me
# ======================================================================
#
#  Build the framework helper dex (javac + d8). Arch-independent: one
#  vdbhelper.dex serves every ABI. Output -> module/vdbhelper.dex.
#  Requires an Android SDK (platform android.jar + build-tools/d8) and a JDK.

set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SDK="${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT:-${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Android/Sdk}}"
AJ="$(ls -d "$SDK"/platforms/android-*/android.jar 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1)"
D8="$(ls -d "$SDK"/build-tools/*/d8 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1)"
[ -f "$AJ" ] || { echo "android.jar not found under $SDK/platforms" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -x "$D8" ] || { echo "d8 not found under $SDK/build-tools" >&2; exit 1; }

OUT="$ROOT/dex/out"; rm -rf "$OUT"; mkdir -p "$OUT"
# shellcheck disable=SC2046
javac --release 11 -cp "$AJ" -d "$OUT" $(find "$ROOT/dex/src" -name '*.java')
# shellcheck disable=SC2046
"$D8" --min-api 26 --lib "$AJ" --output "$ROOT/dex" $(find "$OUT" -name '*.class')
mv "$ROOT/dex/classes.dex" "$ROOT/module/vdbhelper.dex"
rm -rf "$OUT"
echo "built module/vdbhelper.dex ($(wc -c < "$ROOT/module/vdbhelper.dex") bytes)"

`dex/src/ru/vd171/vdbackup/Helper.java`:

```java
/*
 * ======================================================================
 *  VD BACKUP  ::  root backup & restore, no grant prompt
 *  Full app/data backup & restore as root - KernelSU/APatch/Magisk WebUI.
 *
 *  Copyright (C) 2026  VD171
 *  SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 *  Free software under the GNU AGPL v3 or later. NETWORK COPYLEFT: run a
 *  modified version, even as a service, and you MUST offer its source.
 *
 *  Site           : https://vd171.ru
 *  Site           : https://vd.priv8.ru
 *  Source         : https://github.com/VD171/VD-Backup
 *  GitHub         : @VD171 https://github.com/VD171
 *  XDA-Developers : @VD171 https://xdaforums.com/m/vd171.4699873/
 *  XDA-Thread     : https://xdaforums.com/t/VD-Backup.4807267/
 *  Telegram       : @VD_Priv8 https://t.me/VD_Priv8
 *  Telegram       : @Priv8_VD https://t.me/Priv8_VD
 *  Discord        : @VD.Priv8 https://discord.com/users/1296831918989639721
 *  E-mail         : vd.priv8@pm.me
 * ======================================================================
 *
 *  Framework helper run as root via app_process (no installed app):
 *     app_process -Djava.class.path=vdbhelper.dex /system/bin \
 *         ru.vd171.vdbackup.Helper <verb> [args...]
 *  Verbs: list-apps | label <pkg> | icon <pkg> <out.png> | notify <title> <text>
 *  Gives the engine real app labels/icons and reliable notifications. It is the
 *  place the richer framework work (SSAID, AppOps, StorageStats, Neo decrypt) grows.
 *
 *  STATUS: WIP. Compiles + dexes fine. list-apps goes through IPackageManager via
 *  ServiceManager (no ActivityThread/Looper), so it works where systemMain() hangs
 *  (Moto/A16). label/icon/notify still use the systemContext() path. The shell engine
 *  never depends on this (it only uses the dex when present, else falls back), so
 *  shipping without it is safe.
 */
package ru.vd171.vdbackup;

import android.content.Context;
import android.content.pm.ApplicationInfo;
import android.content.pm.PackageInfo;
import android.content.pm.PackageManager;
import android.content.res.AssetManager;
import android.content.res.Resources;
import android.graphics.Bitmap;
import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.Path;
import android.graphics.RectF;
import android.graphics.drawable.Drawable;
import android.os.Build;
import android.os.IBinder;
import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.FileInputStream;
import java.io.FileOutputStream;
import java.io.FileReader;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.lang.reflect.Method;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Base64;
import javax.crypto.Cipher;
import javax.crypto.CipherInputStream;
import javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory;
import javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec;
import javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec;
import javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec;

public final class Helper {

    // system Context from the app_process host (hidden API via reflection, so this
    // compiles against the public android.jar without the hidden-API stubs).
    private static Context systemContext() throws Exception {
        Class<?> at = Class.forName("android.app.ActivityThread");
        Method main = at.getMethod("systemMain");
        Object thread = main.invoke(null);
        Method get = at.getMethod("getSystemContext");
        return (Context) get.invoke(thread);
    }

    // list-apps without ActivityThread/Looper: talk to IPackageManager straight
    // through ServiceManager (both hidden APIs, reached by reflection so this still
    // compiles against the public android.jar). Works where systemMain() hangs.
    private static void listAppsViaServiceManager(int userId) throws Exception {
        Class<?> sm = Class.forName("android.os.ServiceManager");
        IBinder binder = (IBinder) sm.getMethod("getService", String.class).invoke(null, "package");
        if (binder == null) throw new IllegalStateException("package service unavailable");
        Class<?> stub = Class.forName("android.content.pm.IPackageManager$Stub");
        Object ipm = stub.getMethod("asInterface", IBinder.class).invoke(null, binder);

        // getInstalledPackages (not getInstalledApplications): PackageInfo carries the
        // versionCode, which the WebUI uses to key the icon cache so it invalidates when
        // an app updates. applicationInfo is populated by default and gives label/flags.
        Method getPkgs = null;
        for (Method m : ipm.getClass().getMethods()) {
            if ("getInstalledPackages".equals(m.getName()) && m.getParameterTypes().length == 2) {
                getPkgs = m;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (getPkgs == null) throw new NoSuchMethodException("getInstalledPackages");
        Class<?>[] pt = getPkgs.getParameterTypes();
        Object flagsArg = (pt[0] == long.class) ? (Object) 0L : (Object) 0;
        Object slice = getPkgs.invoke(ipm, flagsArg, userId);

        List<?> apps;
        if (slice == null) {
            apps = java.util.Collections.emptyList();
        } else {
            apps = (List<?>) slice.getClass().getMethod("getList").invoke(slice);
        }

        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("{\"ok\":true,\"source\":\"dex\",\"apps\":[");
        boolean first = true;
        for (Object o : apps) {
            PackageInfo pi = (PackageInfo) o;
            ApplicationInfo ai = pi.applicationInfo;
            if (ai == null) continue;
            if (!first) sb.append(',');
            first = false;
            String label = esc(labelOf(ai));
            boolean sys = (ai.flags & ApplicationInfo.FLAG_SYSTEM) != 0;
            long vc = (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 28) ? pi.getLongVersionCode() : (long) pi.versionCode;
            sb.append("{\"package\":\"").append(esc(ai.packageName)).append("\",\"label\":\"")
              .append(label).append("\",\"system\":").append(sys)
              .append(",\"versionCode\":").append(vc).append('}');
        }
        sb.append("]}");
        System.out.println(sb);
    }

    // ApplicationInfo via IPackageManager/ServiceManager (no Context, reflection so it
    // still compiles against public android.jar). Works where systemMain() hangs.
    private static ApplicationInfo appInfo(String pkg, int userId) throws Exception {
        Class<?> sm = Class.forName("android.os.ServiceManager");
        IBinder binder = (IBinder) sm.getMethod("getService", String.class).invoke(null, "package");
        if (binder == null) throw new IllegalStateException("package service unavailable");
        Class<?> stub = Class.forName("android.content.pm.IPackageManager$Stub");
        Object ipm = stub.getMethod("asInterface", IBinder.class).invoke(null, binder);
        Method gai = null;
        for (Method m : ipm.getClass().getMethods()) {
            if ("getApplicationInfo".equals(m.getName()) && m.getParameterTypes().length == 3) { gai = m; break; }
        }
        if (gai == null) throw new NoSuchMethodException("getApplicationInfo");
        Class<?>[] pt = gai.getParameterTypes();
        Object flags = (pt[1] == long.class) ? (Object) 0L : (Object) 0;
        ApplicationInfo ai = (ApplicationInfo) gai.invoke(ipm, pkg, flags, userId);
        if (ai == null) throw new IllegalStateException("no ApplicationInfo for " + pkg);
        return ai;
    }

    // APK resources through a bare AssetManager (no Context, so systemMain() never runs).
    private static Resources apkResources(ApplicationInfo ai) throws Exception {
        String apk = (ai.sourceDir != null) ? ai.sourceDir : ai.publicSourceDir;
        if (apk == null) return null;
        AssetManager am = AssetManager.class.getDeclaredConstructor().newInstance();
        AssetManager.class.getMethod("addAssetPath", String.class).invoke(am, apk);
        return new Resources(am, Resources.getSystem().getDisplayMetrics(),
                             Resources.getSystem().getConfiguration());
    }

    // The real app label: nonLocalizedLabel is null for most apps, so resolve the
    // localized labelRes from the APK's own resources (what getApplicationLabel does).
    private static String labelOf(ApplicationInfo ai) {
        CharSequence nl = ai.nonLocalizedLabel;
        if (nl != null) {
            String s = nl.toString().trim();
            if (!s.isEmpty()) return s;
        }
        if (ai.labelRes != 0) {
            try {
                Resources r = apkResources(ai);
                if (r != null) {
                    String s = r.getString(ai.labelRes);
                    if (s != null && !s.trim().isEmpty()) return s.trim();
                }
            } catch (Throwable ignore) {}
        }
        return ai.packageName;
    }

    // App icon without ActivityThread: get the ApplicationInfo via IPackageManager,
    // load the APK's resources through a bare AssetManager (no Context, so systemMain()
    // never runs), render the icon drawable to a small PNG. Works where the context
    // path hangs. Writes a 144x144 PNG to <out>.
    private static void iconFree(String pkg, String out, int userId) throws Exception {
        ApplicationInfo ai = appInfo(pkg, userId);
        int resId = ai.icon;
        Resources res = apkResources(ai);
        if (resId == 0 || res == null) throw new IllegalStateException("no icon resource");
        Drawable d = res.getDrawable(resId, null);
        if (d == null) throw new IllegalStateException("icon drawable null");
        // Render app-like: a rounded-square mask on every icon for a consistent launcher
        // look. Adaptive icons (API26+) carry a 1/6 bleed per edge meant to be masked off
        // by the launcher; without cropping it the content looks zoomed out, so scale the
        // drawable up to push that bleed past the frame.
        int size = 144;
        Bitmap bmp = Bitmap.createBitmap(size, size, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888);
        Canvas canvas = new Canvas(bmp);
        float r = size * 0.22f;
        Path clip = new Path();
        clip.addRoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, size, size), r, r, Path.Direction.CW);
        canvas.clipPath(clip);
        boolean adaptive = false;
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 26) {
            try { adaptive = Class.forName("android.graphics.drawable.AdaptiveIconDrawable").isInstance(d); }
            catch (Throwable ignore) {}
        }
        if (adaptive) {
            int bleed = size / 6;
            d.setBounds(-bleed, -bleed, size + bleed, size + bleed);
        } else {
            d.setBounds(0, 0, size, size);
        }
        d.draw(canvas);
        try (FileOutputStream fos = new FileOutputStream(out)) {
            bmp.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.PNG, 100, fos);
        }
    }

    // Neo-Backup password crypto: AES/GCM/NoPadding, key = PBKDF2withHmacSHA256
    // (iter=2020, 256-bit), 128-bit tag. Portable (no Keystore), matches upstream
    // CryptoUtils.kt. Decrypts in -> out; the plaintext is still the compressed tar,
    // which the shell engine then decompresses and untars.
    private static byte[] parseIv(String s) {
        s = s.trim();
        if (s.startsWith("[")) {
            String[] parts = s.substring(1, s.length() - 1).split(",");
            byte[] iv = new byte[parts.length];
            for (int i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) iv[i] = (byte) Integer.parseInt(parts[i].trim());
            return iv;
        }
        return Base64.getDecoder().decode(s);
    }

    private static void neoDecrypt(String in, String out, String password, String salt, String ivSpec)
            throws Exception {
        SecretKeyFactory f = SecretKeyFactory.getInstance("PBKDF2withHmacSHA256");
        byte[] key = f.generateSecret(new PBEKeySpec(password.toCharArray(), salt.getBytes("UTF-8"), 2020, 256))
                      .getEncoded();
        Cipher c = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding");
        c.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, new SecretKeySpec(key, "AES"), new GCMParameterSpec(128, parseIv(ivSpec)));
        try (InputStream fis = new FileInputStream(in);
             CipherInputStream cis = new CipherInputStream(fis, c);
             OutputStream fos = new FileOutputStream(out)) {
            byte[] buf = new byte[65536];
            int n;
            while ((n = cis.read(buf)) != -1) fos.write(buf, 0, n);
        }
    }

    private static String esc(String s) {
        if (s == null) return "";
        StringBuilder b = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
            char c = s.charAt(i);
            switch (c) {
                case '"': b.append("\\\""); break;
                case '\\': b.append("\\\\"); break;
                case '\n': b.append("\\n"); break;
                case '\r': b.append("\\r"); break;
                case '\t': b.append("\\t"); break;
                default: if (c < 0x20) b.append(String.format("\\u%04x", (int) c)); else b.append(c);
            }
        }
        return b.toString();
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        try {
            if (args.length == 0) { System.out.println("{\"ok\":false,\"code\":\"ERR_NO_VERB\"}"); return; }
            String verb = args[0];

            // context-free verbs first: never touch ActivityThread (systemMain()
            // hangs on some ROMs) for work that does not need the framework.
            if ("neo-decrypt".equals(verb)) {
                // neo-decrypt <in> <out> <password|-> [salt=oandbackupx] [ivBase64OrArray]
                // password "-" reads VDB_NEO_PASS from the environment (keeps it out of argv/ps).
                String pw = "-".equals(args[3]) ? System.getenv("VDB_NEO_PASS") : args[3];
                if (pw == null) pw = "";
                String salt = (args.length > 4 && args[4].length() > 0) ? args[4] : "oandbackupx";
                String iv = (args.length > 5) ? args[5] : "";
                neoDecrypt(args[1], args[2], pw, salt, iv);
                System.out.println("{\"ok\":true,\"verb\":\"neo-decrypt\",\"out\":\"" + esc(args[2]) + "\"}");
                System.out.flush();
                System.exit(0);
                return;
            }

            if ("list-apps".equals(verb)) {
                int userId = 0;
                if (args.length > 1) { try { userId = Integer.parseInt(args[1]); } catch (NumberFormatException ignore) { } }
                listAppsViaServiceManager(userId);
                System.out.flush();
                System.exit(0);
                return;
            }

            if ("icon".equals(verb)) {
                // icon <pkg> <out.png> [userId] - context-free, never hangs
                int userId = 0;
                if (args.length > 3) { try { userId = Integer.parseInt(args[3]); } catch (NumberFormatException ignore) { } }
                iconFree(args[1], args[2], userId);
                System.out.println("{\"ok\":true,\"icon\":\"" + esc(args[2]) + "\"}");
                System.out.flush();
                System.exit(0);
                return;
            }

            if ("icons".equals(verb)) {
                // icons <userId> <listfile> - batch: one JVM renders many icons.
                // listfile: one "pkg\t/abs/out.png" per line. Amortizes JVM startup.
                int userId = 0;
                try { userId = Integer.parseInt(args[1]); } catch (Exception ignore) { }
                int rendered = 0; StringBuilder failed = new StringBuilder();
                try (BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(args[2]))) {
                    String line;
                    while ((line = br.readLine()) != null) {
                        int t = line.indexOf('\t');
                        if (t <= 0) continue;
                        String pkg = line.substring(0, t), out = line.substring(t + 1);
                        try { iconFree(pkg, out, userId); rendered++; }
                        catch (Throwable e) { if (failed.length() > 0) failed.append(','); failed.append('"').append(esc(pkg)).append('"'); }
                    }
                }
                System.out.println("{\"ok\":true,\"rendered\":" + rendered + ",\"failed\":[" + failed + "]}");
                System.out.flush();
                System.exit(0);
                return;
            }

            if ("label".equals(verb)) {
                // label <pkg> [userId] - context-free, never hangs
                int userId = 0;
                if (args.length > 2) { try { userId = Integer.parseInt(args[2]); } catch (NumberFormatException ignore) { } }
                System.out.println("{\"ok\":true,\"label\":\"" + esc(labelOf(appInfo(args[1], userId))) + "\"}");
                System.out.flush();
                System.exit(0);
                return;
            }

            Context ctx = systemContext();

            if ("notify".equals(verb)) {
                // best-effort; cmd notification is the primary path in the shell engine
                Object nm = ctx.getSystemService("notification");
                System.out.println("{\"ok\":" + (nm != null) + ",\"verb\":\"notify\"}");

            } else {
                System.out.println("{\"ok\":false,\"code\":\"ERR_UNKNOWN_VERB\"}");
            }
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            System.out.println("{\"ok\":false,\"code\":\"ERR_DEX\",\"message\":\"" + esc(t.toString()) + "\"}");
        }
        // ActivityThread leaves non-daemon threads alive; force exit so app_process returns.
        System.out.flush();
        System.exit(0);
    }
}

```

# Driving VDBackup from an AI agent

VDBackup is built so an AI assistant or agent can administer **every** content and
action of the module headlessly, the same way a person does through the WebUI. The
WebUI is just one client of a small JSON API; your agent is another. Use the API,
do not scrape the WebUI.

## The contract

Everything goes through one entry point, run as root on the device:

```
sh /data/adb/modules/vdbackup/scripts/helper.sh <verb> <base64(JSON-args)>
```

- Arguments are a single JSON object, **base64-encoded**, passed as one argv token.
- The command prints **one JSON object** on stdout: `{"ok":true,...}` or
  `{"ok":false,"code":"ERR_...","message":"..."}`. Parse that; never scrape text.
- Long operations (`backup`, `restore`, `import`) return `{"ok":true,"opid":"..."}`
  immediately and run **detached** (they survive the caller/WebUI going away). Poll
  their progress; they are not finished when the call returns.
- `progress` and `cancel` take **base64 of the raw opid string**, not a JSON object.

A tiny helper for your shell:

```sh
b64() { printf '%s' "$1" | base64 -w0; }
H=/data/adb/modules/vdbackup/scripts/helper.sh
sh "$H" backup "$(b64 '{"package":"com.example.app","mode":"full"}')"
```

To drive it from a workstation, run that over your usual root channel to the device
(adb shell as root, or an SSH-to-root setup). The module ships bundled binaries, so
once installed it needs **no internet** for local backup/restore; only cloud
destinations (`rclone`/`restic`/ssh) talk to the network.

## Verbs

| Verb | Args (JSON) | Returns |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `ping` | `{}` | `{ok,version,abi}` |
| `overview` | `{user?}` | `{ok:true,apps,instances,path_backups,jobs,backups_size,free,total}` counts (sizes in bytes): apps with backups, total backup instances, standalone path backups, scheduled jobs, total backups size, and the backups filesystem free/total. Non-detached, returns immediately; used by the WebUI home overview. |
| `config-get` | `{}` | `{ok,config}` |
| `config-set` | the config object (or `{key,value}`) | `{ok}` |
| `keygen` | `{}` | generates the `age` keypair for encryption |
| `list-apps` | `{user?}` | `{ok,apps:[{package,label,system,versionCode}]}` (dex, shell fallback) |
| `label` | `{package,user?}` | `{ok,label}` (real localized app name, context-free) |
| `icon` | `{package,user?,vc?}` | `{ok,package,icon}` (base64 PNG; cached per package+`vc`) |
| `backup` | see below | `{ok,opid}` (detached) |
| `restore` | see below | `{ok,opid}` (detached) |
| `import` | `{from,ref,password,ssaid,user}` | `{ok,opid}` (detached) |
| `import-scan` | `{from,path}` | `{ok,backups:[...]}` |
| `progress` | base64(opid) | the live `progress-<opid>.json` |
| `cancel` | base64(opid) | `{ok,cancelled}` |
| `list-ops` | `{}` | `{ok,ops:[...]}` (reattach after reconnecting) |
| `list-apps`/`icons` | `{user?}` / `{user?,items:[{package,vc}]}` | app list / batch base64 icons |
| `list-backups` | `{package?}` | `{ok,backups:[{ref,package,label,versionName,versionCode,created_at,mode,items}]}` |
| `backup-info` | `{ref}` | `{ok,...}` one backup's full details (version, install source, state, date, mode, size, items, permission counts, device) |
| `backup-icon` | `{ref}` | `{ok,icon}` base64 PNG from the manifest (works when the app is uninstalled) |
| `delete-backup` | `{ref}` | `{ok,deleted}` (ref must be under the backups dir) |
| `prune` | `{package,user?,keep}` | `{ok,pruned:[...]}` keep newest N of a package |
| `log-read` | `{limit?}` | `{ok,entries:[...]}` audit log, newest first |
| `log-export` | `{user?}` | `{ok:true,path}` (absolute path of a written `.txt` under the backups dir) or `{ok:false,code:"ERR_LOG_EXPORT"}`. Writes the activity log (`audit.jsonl`) plus a short build/device header to a single user-visible text file so it can be attached to a bug report. Non-detached, returns immediately. |
| `special-categories` | `{}` | `{ok,categories:[{id,available}]}` (messages/contacts/wifi/bluetooth/calendar/wallpaper/dns/system_settings) |
| `special-backup` | `{categories,compression?,password?,portable?}` | `{ok,opid}` system-wide backup (detached) |
| `special-restore` | `{ref,confirm:true,categories?,password?}` | `{ok,opid}` (reboot-required; `confirm` gates it) |
| `special-list` | `{}` | `{ok,backups:[{ref,created_at,categories}]}` |
| `path-backup` | `{path,compression?,password?}` | `{ok,opid}` back up any absolute path as `tar.zst`+`manifest.json` under `.paths/` (detached) |
| `path-restore` | `{ref,confirm:true,password?}` | `{ok,opid}` restore a path backup to its original location (`confirm` gates it; detached) |
| `sysmount-status` | `{}` | `{ok,nomount,nm,ksu,live_capable}` |
| `sysmount-add` / `sysmount-del` / `sysmount-list` | `{package,priv?}` | mount an installed app as a system app (systemless sub-module; live via NoMount else next boot) |
| `companion-status` / `companion-install` | `{}` | Google Drive companion status / on-demand install |
| `dests-list` / `dest-add` / `dest-test` / `dest-del` | `{id,type,...}` | destination management |
| `remote-add` / `remote-list` / `remote-del` | `{name,backend,params:{...}}` | rclone remote management (creates the `rclone.conf` entry a `type:"rclone"` dest points to); `backend` may be any rclone backend, no whitelist |
| `remote-authorize` | `{backend}` | `{ok:true,url}` (the engine already opened the phone browser to that consent URL via an Android VIEW intent) or `{ok:false,code:"ERR_AUTHORIZE"}`. Runs `rclone authorize <backend>` on a local callback server (`127.0.0.1:53682`) for on-device OAuth. |
| `remote-authorize-poll` | `{}` | `{ok:true,done:false,url}` while waiting, `{ok:true,done:true,token}` once the user consented (the `token` to pass to `remote-add`), or `{ok:false,code:"ERR_AUTHORIZE"}`. |
| `remote-authorize-cancel` | `{}` | `{ok:true,cancelled:true}`; stops a pending authorization. |
| `cloud-status` | `{}` | `{ok,rclone,restic,fetchable,size}` (are the `rclone`/`restic` binaries present, can this `lite` edition fetch them, download size in bytes) |
| `cloud-fetch` | `{}` | `{ok,opid}` (detached) fetch+verify+install the `rclone`/`restic` addon on a `lite` edition |
| `schedule-set` / `schedule-list` / `schedule-delete` | see below | scheduled jobs (a backup or a restore; targeting one app, a set, or all apps) |
| `scheduler-tick` | `{}` | runs due jobs + applies retention + the auto-backup observer (the boot heartbeat calls this) |
| `update-check` | `{}` | `{ok,current_version,current_code,latest_version,latest_code,update_available,zipUrl,changelog,notes}` (not detached; returns immediately; `ERR_UPDATE_CHECK` on failure - see below) |

### `progress` fields

Polling `progress` returns the live `progress-<opid>.json` for the operation. These fields
are **always present**:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| `opid` | string | the operation id |
| `percent` | int | 0-100 completion |
| `phase` | string | current phase label |
| `item` | string | current item type being processed |
| `done` | bool | true on a terminal write (finish / dry-run / restore-test) |

A running operation may also carry these **optional** live fields. They are absent or empty
when unknown, and are **omitted on terminal writes** (finish / dry-run / restore-test):

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| `rate` | string | transfer speed, e.g. `"4.2 MiB/s"` (empty = unknown) |
| `eta` | string | estimated time remaining, e.g. `"1m12s"` (empty = unknown) |
| `n` | int | current item index (0 = unknown) |
| `of` | int | total item count (0 = unknown) |
| `cur` | string | current item name (empty = none) |

Cloud transfers populate `rate`/`eta` (the percent comes from rclone); local Full backups
populate `n`/`of`/`cur`. Phase labels include the checksum-seal phase **`verified`** and,
for cloud transfers, **`transfer`** and **`mirror <item>`**.

### `backup` args

```json
{
  "package": "com.example.app",
  "user": 0,
  "mode": "full",                 // full | snapshot | mirror
  "compression": "zstd:10",       // none | lz4 | zstd[:N] | gzip
  "items": ["apk","data","data_de","obb","external","media"],
  "encrypt_data": false,
  "encrypt_apk": false,
  "dest": "local",                // local | <destination id>
  "verify": true,                 // re-hash each archive vs the manifest (default on for Full)
  "dry_run": false,               // true = report a size plan, write nothing
  "ssaid": false                  // OPT-IN, see below
}
```

`restore`/`import` take `{ref}` (a backup dir / scan ref). `restore` also accepts:
`"items"` (a subset of the backup's item types to restore; omit for all), `"test": true`
(extract to a temp dir and verify, without touching the live app), `"mode"` for
snapshot/mirror, `"password"` for an encrypted backup, `"ssaid"` (opt-in), and the
install-source options `"spoof_installer"` (default from config, sets the installer to the
Play Store at install time) and `"deep_spoof": true` (advanced opt-in; also forges the
initiating package and package source by editing the package database, applies after a
reboot). `import` takes `"from": "neo" | "databackup"` and, for an encrypted Neo backup,
`"password"`.

### `schedule-set` args

A schedule job picks **one** target and an **action**:

```json
{
  "id": "nightly-games",
  "action": "backup",             // "backup" (default) | "restore"
  "package": "com.example.app",   // one app   - OR -
  "packages": ["com.a","com.b"],  // a set of apps   - OR -
  "all": true,                    // all apps, minus the excluded-apps list
  "cron": "daily",                // hourly | daily | weekly
  "at": "02:30",                  // HH:MM
  "mode": "full",
  "dest": "local",
  "keep": 5,
  "items": ["apk","data"],
  "require_wifi": false,          // gate: only run on Wi-Fi
  "require_charging": false,      // gate: only run while charging
  "min_battery": 0,               // gate: only run at/above this battery % (0-100)
  "days": [1,2,3,4,5]             // gate: only run on these weekdays (0=Sunday)
}
```

Give exactly **one** of `package`, `packages` or `all` for the target. A `backup` job
keeps the usual `mode`/`dest`/`keep`/`items`. A `restore` job (`action: "restore"`)
restores each target app's **latest** backup (or an explicit `ref`) and **overwrites the
app's current data on every run** - it is deliberate and opt-in, so set it only on a
direct user request.

### Scheduler gating

A scheduled job may carry **optional gate conditions**. When a due job's gate is not met it
is **skipped and retried on the next tick, without advancing its schedule** (its `last_run`
is not stamped, so it fires as soon as the condition holds):

| Field | Type | Gate |
|-------|------|------|
| `require_wifi` | bool | only run while on Wi-Fi |
| `require_charging` | bool | only run while charging |
| `min_battery` | int (0-100) | only run at or above this battery level |
| `days` | array of int (0-6, 0=Sunday) | only run on these weekdays |

A minimal **thermal safety** check is always applied on top of these: a scheduled op is
skipped while the device is critically hot. Every gate skip is written to the audit trail as
`op:"scheduler-gated"` with a `reason` of `wifi` / `charging` / `battery` / `days` /
`thermal`.

### `remote-add` args

A cloud destination is a `type:"rclone"` dest that names an `rclone` remote; create
that remote first with `remote-add`. The `backend` may be **any rclone backend** - there
is no whitelist. `remote-add` accepts any backend name (`dropbox`, `onedrive`, `box`,
`pcloud`, `mega`, `b2`, `s3`, `sftp`, `smb`, `webdav`, `ftp`, `drive` and the ~70 others
rclone supports), and the `params` are passed straight through to the `rclone` config as
`key=value` pairs. Password fields are stored obscured, never in clear. Common backends
and their `params`:

```
sftp   : host, port, user, pass           smb  : host, port, user, pass
ftp    : host, port, user, pass           webdav: url, vendor, user, pass
s3     : provider, access_key_id, secret_access_key, endpoint, region
drive  : token, scope                     (token = output of `rclone authorize "drive"`)
```

**On-device OAuth (no PC).** Backends that need a browser sign-in (Google Drive, Dropbox,
OneDrive, Box, pCloud) do not require a desktop or a manually pasted token. Call
`remote-authorize` with `{backend}`: the engine runs `rclone authorize <backend>` against a
local callback server (`127.0.0.1:53682`) and opens the phone's own browser at the provider
consent page via an Android VIEW intent, returning `{ok:true,url}` (or
`{ok:false,code:"ERR_AUTHORIZE"}`). Poll `remote-authorize-poll` (`{}`): it returns
`{ok:true,done:false,url}` while waiting and `{ok:true,done:true,token}` once the user
approves - pass that `token` to `remote-add`. `remote-authorize-cancel` (`{}`) stops a
pending authorization (`{ok:true,cancelled:true}`). Manually pasting the output of
`rclone authorize "<backend>"` from any computer is still supported as a fallback.

Google Drive has two paths: this `drive` remote (no Google Cloud project needed, uses
rclone's own OAuth - authorize on-device with `remote-authorize`, or run
`rclone authorize "drive"` once on any computer and pass the token) or the opt-in companion
app (your own OAuth client id). Both end up as ordinary destinations.

### Network policy

The config field `network_policy` controls which connection cloud transfers may use:
`any` (default), `wifi`, or `mobile`. Set it with `config-set`. When it is `wifi` or
`mobile`, every cloud transfer (Full `rclone`/Drive upload, Mirror sync, remote
`restic` snapshot backup/restore, Mirror restore) checks the active transport first and
aborts with `ERR_NET_POLICY` if it does not match - for both manual and scheduled jobs.
Local destinations are never gated.

### Cloud integrity and quota

- **Checksum seal (cloud).** After a successful cloud copy the engine runs a remote checksum
  check (`rclone check`); a mismatch fails the op with `ERR_VERIFY`. Backends that share no
  common hash with the local side are skipped (not a failure).
- **Quota check (cloud, Full mode).** Before a Full-mode upload to an `rclone` remote the
  engine queries the remote's free space (`rclone about --json`) and refuses with
  `ERR_QUOTA` if the backup would not fit. Remotes that report no quota information are
  skipped. Mirror mode is a delta sync and is exempt.

### Cloud binaries (`lite` edition)

A `full` edition bundles every binary and never needs the network. The `lite` edition omits
the two largest, `rclone` and `restic`, and fetches them on demand the first time you run a
cloud or snapshot action. `cloud-status` reports whether they are already present, whether this
edition can fetch them, and the download size in bytes. `cloud-fetch` runs **detached** (poll
`progress` with its `opid`): it downloads the per-architecture `rclone`+`restic` addon, verifies
it against the SHA-256 baked into the module, and installs it into the runtime cache. Its
progress phases are `downloading`, `verifying`, and `installing`; the final code is `ERR_NONE`
on success, or `ERR_FETCH` (download failed) / `ERR_FETCH_VERIFY` (checksum mismatch, discarded)
on failure. On a `full` edition it is unnecessary. A `backup`/`restore` to a cloud or snapshot
destination on the `lite` edition, before the binaries are present, fails with
`ERR_CLOUD_FETCHABLE`; the client should offer to run `cloud-fetch`, then retry.

### Special backup categories

`special-categories` reports which system-wide categories a device has; `special-backup`
captures the ones you pass in `categories` and `special-restore` re-applies them. The
categories are:

| Category | What it is | Restore semantics |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|
| `messages` | SMS/MMS | provider replace (wipe + extract) |
| `contacts` | contacts and call log | provider replace (wipe + extract) |
| `wifi` | saved Wi-Fi networks | provider replace (wipe + extract) |
| `bluetooth` | Bluetooth pairings | provider replace (wipe + extract) |
| `calendar` | the calendar provider (`com.android.providers.calendar`, app + data); also exported portably to `calendar.json` | provider replace (wipe + extract) |
| `wallpaper` | home and lock wallpaper plus `wallpaper_info.xml`, stored raw (binary) | files replaced |
| `dns` | the private DNS mode and specifier, read from settings | idempotent `settings put` |
| `system_settings` | the full system/global/secure settings dump | **opt-in**, idempotent `settings put`, overwrites device settings |

**`system_settings` is strictly opt-in and destructive on restore.** Like `ssaid`, it
overwrites device-wide settings when it is restored, so it is gated behind explicit user
consent and written to the audit trail. Never select it by default; only on a direct,
deliberate user request.

### Standalone path backup

`path-backup` / `path-restore` back up and restore **any absolute path** - a folder or a
single file - on shared storage or under `/data`, outside the per-app model. The archive
is written as `tar.zst` plus a `manifest.json` in VDBackup's own format (SHA-256 sealed,
with a RECOVERY kit when encrypted) under `.paths/` in the backups directory.

```json
// path-backup
{ "path": "/sdcard/DCIM/Camera", "compression": "zstd:10", "password": "..." }
// path-restore
{ "ref": "<.paths ref>", "confirm": true, "password": "..." }
```

- The source path must be **absolute** and under one of the allowed roots:
  `/storage/emulated`, `/data/media`, `/sdcard`, `/data`. A path that does not exist fails
  with `ERR_NO_PATH`; a path outside the allowed roots, or one containing `..`, fails with
  `ERR_BAD_PATH`.
- `path-restore` writes back to the original location, so it is destructive and requires
  `"confirm": true` - a heavy-friction gate, like `special-restore`. A `ref` that is not a
  valid path backup fails with `ERR_BAD_REF`.
- Both run **detached**; poll `progress` with the returned `opid`.

### `update-check`

`update-check` reports whether a newer version of the module has been published, so an agent
(or the WebUI) can surface it. It is a **read verb that returns immediately** - it is **not**
detached, so there is no `opid` to poll. Triggered only by an explicit user action, it fetches
the module's published update manifest (the `updateJson` URL from `module.prop`) with the bundled
`curl` over a root-side HTTP request - this runs outside the WebView, so it is not subject to the
WebUI CSP - and compares the published `versionCode` with the installed one. It takes **no
arguments**.

On success it returns:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| `ok` | bool | `true` |
| `current_version` | string | the installed versionName |
| `current_code` | int | the installed versionCode |
| `latest_version` | string | the published versionName |
| `latest_code` | int | the published versionCode |
| `update_available` | bool | `true` when `latest_code` is greater than `current_code` |
| `zipUrl` | string | the published zip URL |
| `changelog` | string | the published changelog URL |
| `notes` | string | the release notes |

If there is no `updateJson` URL, the network request fails, or the manifest cannot be parsed, it
returns `{"ok":false,"code":"ERR_UPDATE_CHECK"}`.

`update-check` only **reports** availability and release notes; the update itself is performed by
your root manager (KernelSU / APatch / Magisk) through the module's `updateJson`, never by this
verb.

## Safety rails your agent must respect

- **`ssaid` is strictly opt-in (default off).** It backs up / restores the device
  ANDROID_ID by rewriting a system file; a restore applies only after a reboot, and
  the previous file is always saved first for rollback. Only send `"ssaid": true`
  on a direct, deliberate user request - never by default.
- **Mutating actions (restore, delete, import) are destructive** and are logged to a
  local audit trail (`logs/audit.jsonl`). Restore is faithful (wipe-then-extract), so
  it reverts the app to the backup's exact state. Confirm intent before you call them.
- **`system_settings` is opt-in and destructive, exactly like `ssaid`.** Restoring it
  overwrites device-wide settings, so send it only on a direct user request; it is gated
  by explicit consent and recorded in the audit trail.
- **Restore is idempotent.** Raw provider restores (messages/contacts/wifi/bluetooth/
  calendar) **replace** rather than merge - the provider data is wiped and the archive is
  extracted over it - so re-restoring the same backup cannot duplicate rows. `dns` and
  `system_settings` are re-applied with idempotent `settings put`.
- **Archive extraction is guarded against path traversal.** Restore runs as root, so
  every archive (restore, import, special-restore, path-restore) is checked before any
  write: one whose members use absolute paths or contain `..` is rejected up front with
  `ERR_UNSAFE_ARCHIVE`, before a single destructive write happens (GNU tar also runs with
  `--no-absolute-names`). A tampered archive can never escape its target directory.
- **Never weaken** preservation (SELinux/uid/gid/modes/xattr) or the APK rule (APKs
  are always compressed, never encrypted unless `encrypt_apk` is set).
- Treat the JSON output as the source of truth; check `ok`/`code`, poll `progress`,
  and surface `ERR_*` codes rather than guessing.

See [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[FILE-STRUCTURE.md](FILE-STRUCTURE.md) for the internals.

# Architecture

VDBackup is a root WebUI module. It has three layers: the **WebUI** (what you see),
the **shell backend** (what does the work, as root), and the **bundled binaries**
(the archivers and transports). Everything runs already-root, so there is no
permission prompt and no companion app for the core features.

```
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  WebUI  (module/webroot, vanilla JS)                      │
   │    index.html · scripts.js · i18n.js · styles.css         │
   │    lang/en.js + 21 languages · config.json (CSP, no net)  │
   └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                   │  ksu.exec("sh scripts/helper.sh <verb> <b64json>")
                   ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  scripts/helper.sh  (dispatcher, returns JSON)            │
   │    list-apps · config · dests · backup/restore/import ... │
   │    long ops -> setsid nohup scripts/worker.sh  (detached) │
   └───────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬──────────┘
                   │                               │ progress-<opid>.json (poll)
                   ▼                               ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────┐
   │  scripts/worker.sh (root, detached)│   │  framework helper (opt.) │
   │   force-stop · tar|zstd|age        │   │  app_process + dex       │
   │   pm install · chown/chcon         │   │  perms/appops/ssaid/...  │
   │   transfer · notify                │   │  (dex primary, shell fb) │
   └───────────────┬────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────┘
                   ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  bin/<abi>/  tar · zstd · lz4 · rclone · rsync · ssh · restic │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                   ▼
   Destinations: local · SFTP/SCP · SMB · WebDAV · FTP · S3 · 70+ (rclone)
                 rsync · restic repos · Google Drive (opt-in companion)
```

## Key points

- **Already root.** The module process is root, so the engine is plain shell. ~85% of
  the work is pure shell (`tar`/`zstd`/`age`/`pm`/`am`/`chown`/`chcon`/`rclone`/...).
- **Detached execution.** Backup/restore run via `setsid nohup`, as an independent root
  process. Closing the WebUI does not interrupt them; the UI reattaches by reading
  `logs/progress-<opid>.json`.
- **Framework helper (~15%).** Fine-grained permissions, AppOps, SSAID, StorageStats,
  icons and privileged Wi-Fi need the Android framework. A small `dex` run via
  `app_process` (no installed app) handles these, with a shell fallback.
- **Portability.** Only standard formats; backups open on a PC without this module.
- **State** lives in `/data/adb/vdbackup/` (config, jobs, destinations, encrypted
  credentials, logs, staging). **Backups** are written to user-visible, credential-
  encrypted storage at `/sdcard/VDBackup/` (`/data/media/<user>/VDBackup`, per user),
  not in `/data/adb` (which is device-encrypted and readable before first unlock).

## Compatibility guarantee

A backup must stay restorable forever. This is a hard rule, not a best effort.

**Scope.** The guarantee covers backups written by **v1.01 onward** (the first officially
published release) and only by officially published, released versions. v1.00 was a
test-only build and is explicitly out of scope; pre-release and development builds are not
covered. From the first public release forward, the promise below is absolute:

- **Standard formats only.** Every archive is a plain `tar` compressed with `zstd`,
  `gzip` or `lz4`, optionally wrapped with `age`. There is no proprietary container, so
  a backup can be opened on any PC with ordinary tools even without this module (see
  `etc/RECOVERY.md`). A format we cannot drop.
- **Append-only metadata.** `manifest.json` carries `format_version`. The schema only
  ever grows: fields may be *added*, never removed, renamed or repurposed. Restore reads
  every field defensively (missing optional fields fall back to a default) and installs
  APKs and extracts archives by their file name and extension, not by assuming a fixed
  manifest shape.
- **Forward compatible restore.** Restore never rejects a backup for being old, and an
  older VDBackup silently skips item types it does not know rather than failing. A newer
  VDBackup therefore restores any older backup, and the standard-format archives remain
  restorable by hand regardless.

In short: anything VDBackup has ever written, every future VDBackup (and a plain PC)
can still restore. Changing the format in a way that breaks a prior backup is not
allowed; new capabilities are added behind `format_version` and new, additive fields.

For the full technical design (archive format, metadata schema, pipelines, crypto,
destinations, importers) the maintainers keep detailed design notes; this file is the
contributor-facing overview.

# Bundled binaries: provenance and auditing

Privacy and security are not optional in VDBackup. A backup tool runs as root over
your most personal data, so you must be able to see exactly what ships inside it. This
page documents every prebuilt binary and library the module carries, where each comes
from, and how to verify that nothing opaque was slipped in.

## Principles

- **Nothing opaque.** Every shipped binary and library is traceable to a named, public
  upstream at a pinned version, with a recorded SHA-256. No blob is bundled without an
  entry you can check.
- **Fetched from upstream, never from a device.** Native tools come from the official
  Termux package repository (the signed `.deb` files at `packages.termux.dev/apt`), never
  copied out of a Termux installed on some phone. The build fails loudly, it never
  improvises.
- **Reproducible.** Re-run the build and you get the same files; re-fetch the pinned
  sources and the SHA-256 values match.
- **The audit trail ships with the module.** It is not just on the website - it travels
  inside the installed module, on your device, so you can audit offline.

## What ships, and from where

| Artifact | Source | How it is built |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/<abi>/` native tools (`tar`, `zstd`, `gzip`, `lz4`, `jq`, `rclone`, `restic`, `rsync`, `ssh`/`scp`/`sftp`, `age`, `age-keygen`, `script`, `sqlite3`) + their `lib/` closure | Official **Termux** apt repo (`packages.termux.dev/apt`), official `.deb` packages | `.github/scripts/build_bin.sh` downloads the `.deb` files + their transitive dependencies, extracts them, and copies the binaries plus only the shared libraries each one needs |
| `bin/<abi>/abx2xml`, `bin/<abi>/xml2abx` (ABX converter fallback) | **rhythmcache/android-xml-converter** GitHub release (`ABX_RELEASE`, static ELF) | downloaded from the pinned release by `build_bin.sh` |
| `companion.apk` (optional Google Drive companion) | **This repository**, `companion/` (Gradle/Kotlin) | built from source by CI and signed with the project key (`VD_Key`); not a prebuilt blob |
| `vdbhelper.dex` (framework helper) | **This repository**, `dex/src/` (Java) | compiled from source by CI with `javac` + `d8` |

Only the first two rows are prebuilt third-party binaries; the last two are built from
source that lives in this repository and can be read and rebuilt.

> **Full vs lite editions.** The lite editions omit only `rclone` and `restic` (the
> two largest binaries) to stay small and fetch them on demand (SHA-256-verified) the
> first time you use a cloud destination or snapshot mode; `rsync` and `ssh`/`scp`/`sftp`
> are still present, and every other binary listed above is present too. The full editions
> ship `rclone` (cloud providers) and `restic` (snapshots) embedded, so nothing is ever
> downloaded.

## The on-device manifest: `PROVENANCE.json`

`build_bin.sh` writes one `bin/<abi>/PROVENANCE.json` per ABI. On install the module
keeps only your device's ABI, so that file stays on the device at
`/data/adb/modules/vdbackup/bin/<abi>/PROVENANCE.json`. It records:

- `sources`: every upstream `.deb` (package, version, full URL, SHA-256 of the `.deb`) and
  the ABX release (URL, SHA-256 of the archive).
- `files`: every file actually shipped under `bin/<abi>/` (path, size, SHA-256).

You can read it in the WebUI (the **About** tab links to it) or over the agent API:

```sh
sh /data/adb/modules/vdbackup/helper.sh provenance '' | jq .
```

## How to verify (step by step)

1. **Check the shipped files.** Hash each file under `bin/<abi>/` on your device and
   compare to the `files[].sha256` in `PROVENANCE.json`:
   ```sh
   cd /data/adb/modules/vdbackup/bin/<abi>
   sha256sum tar zstd jq rclone ... lib/*
   ```
2. **Check the files against upstream.** For each `sources[]` entry, download the pinned
   `.deb` from its URL, confirm its SHA-256 matches `deb_sha256`, extract it, and confirm
   the binaries/libraries it contains hash to the same values shipped. The `.deb` files in
   the Termux repo are themselves served from Termux's signed apt repository.
3. **Rebuild from scratch.** Run `.github/scripts/build_bin.sh` yourself (needs only
   `curl`, `ar`, `tar`, `xz`, `zstd`, `readelf`) and compare the output to what shipped.
4. **Companion and dex.** Rebuild `companion/` and `dex/` from source; the companion's
   signature is the project key `VD_Key` (SHA-256
   `F3:F8:2B:B9:2F:2C:69:A1:75:90:1D:40:BD:65:DD:A6:8F:2B:B5:88:69:77:F5:EA:8B:BA:AA:51:40:E5:25:2B`).

## Reporting

If any shipped file does not match its recorded source, treat it as a security issue and
report it (see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)). This is exactly the kind of discrepancy this
manifest exists to make visible.

# VDBackup user guide

A complete, friendly walkthrough of VDBackup, from installing the module to making
your first backup, restoring it, sending it to the cloud, scheduling it, and opening
it on a PC years later. If you have used Swift Backup, Neo-Backup or
Android-DataBackup before, this will feel familiar - only everything happens in one
place, with nothing to "allow".
